answer.rationale: Current situation shows activation down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4% QoQ. Memory_31 and memory_91 directly address activation lift through different mechanisms—simplification and in-product messaging respectively. Verification of these two will clarify whether the decline stems from friction in signup/onboarding (suggesting simplify_onboarding) or from weak engagement signals post-onboarding (suggesting activation_messaging). Memory_91 (in-product activation messaging) is the highest-leverage candidate because: (1) it directly targets the stated activation decline, (2) it has no documented retention risk unlike promotional_pricing (memory_73 showed 12-point retention loss), (3) it complements the onboarding improvements already proven (memory_86), and (4) it can be deployed quickly without pricing or acquisition channel changes that might conflict with enterprise sales strategy. Promotional_pricing is rejected because memory_73 shows it trades long-term retention for short-term volume—misaligned with sustainable qualified revenue objective. Referral_incentive (memory_57) is lower urgency since it works best on established customers, not addressing the current churn in activation metrics. Enterprise_sales_assist, while valuable, does not address the SMB activation crisis. A standard_experiment on activation_messaging preserves optionality: success unlocks a quick win; failure signals we need to revisit onboarding simplification or pricing strategy next cycle.
